lines: A drum voice built from a tuned tone oscillator and a noise generator, crossfaded together and shaped by one envelope, after Bastl's Crust module
Sets the octave of the tone oscillator over a ten-octave range, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Octave
Sets the pitch envelope: clockwise gives a falling kick-style sweep, counter-clockwise a slower membrane sweep, and this is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Sweep
Detunes the second oscillator from the first: counter-clockwise by a fixed number of Hz, down into LFO speeds and independent of the pitch, clockwise by an exponential ratio reaching 16 to 1
Tunes the ratio between the two oscillators in fractions of an interval, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Stepped Detune
Shifts the tone oscillator by up to 12 semitones either way, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Semitone
Shifts the tone oscillator by up to 1 semitone either way, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Fine
Sweeps the tone oscillator smoothly across its whole frequency range, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Broad
Sets the pitch of the noise layer, which each noise algorithm reads its own way, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Noise Param
Steps the PITCH knob to the next tune mode on each press; a long press swaps between the octave, sweep and detune set and the tune, semitone and fine-tune set, and a second long press leaves that
Crossfades the output between the tone layer and the noise layer
Steps the tone oscillator to the next mode on each press, through Dual, Ring Mod, FM and FM 2; a long press moves the PITCH knob onto the stepped detune and the ENV knob onto the pitch envelope decay
Sets the amplitude envelope applied to both the tone and the noise layer: clockwise lengthens the decay, counter-clockwise lengthens attack and decay together
Sets the decay time of the pitch envelope, shortest at the centre and following a different exponential curve to each side; this is what the ENV knob does after a long press of the tone mode button
Steps the noise generator to the next algorithm on each press, through Noise, Crunch, Metal and Clap; a long press moves the PITCH knob onto the noise tuning
Drives the voice into distortion, and is what the TIMBRE fader does while the timbre mode is Distortion
Sets the filter cutoff applied to the noise layer alone, and is what the TIMBRE fader does while the timbre mode is Filter
Reshapes the tone oscillator's waveform, and is what the TIMBRE fader does while the timbre mode is Shape
Steps the TIMBRE fader to the next timbre mode on each press, through Distortion, Filter and Shape; a long press starts choosing what the CTRL knob is assigned to
Sets whichever one parameter the control destination names, and adds to the voltage at the CTRL input when a cable is patched there
Adds to whatever the TIMBRE fader is set to at the moment, -5V to 5V covering the full travel of that fader
Adds to the LAYER fader, -5V to 5V covering the full crossfade between tone and noise
Adds to the CTRL knob, -5V to 5V covering the full range of whatever the control destination names
Scales the loudness of the hit, 0V silent and 10V full, and negative voltages read as 0V; with TRIG unpatched a voltage here fires the voice as well, above 1.5V to sound and back below 0.5V to rearm
Fires the drum on each rising edge past 1V
Sets the pitch of the tone oscillator, doubling its frequency for each volt
Adds to the ENV knob, -5V to 5V covering the full range of that knob
The amplitude envelope of the voice as a voltage, 0V at rest and 5V at the peak of a hit
The drum itself, the tone and noise layers crossfaded and enveloped, reaching 5V either way
Note — nothing sounds until a trigger arrives at TRIG; with TRIG unpatched a gate at VELOCITY fires the voice instead, and with neither patched the module is silent
Note — fourteen factory presets are installed with the plugin, reached from the module's right-click menu under Preset
Menu — Module Modes — a submenu gathering the four mode settings the panel buttons step through
Menu — Tune Mode: Octave, Sweep, Detune, Stepped Detune, Semitone, Fine, Broad, Noise Param — sets what the PITCH knob adjusts; inside Module Modes
Menu — Tone Mode: Dual, Ring Mod, FM, FM 2 — sets how the two oscillators of the tone layer combine; inside Module Modes
Menu — Noise Mode: Noise, Crunch, Metal, Clap — sets the noise algorithm; inside Module Modes
Menu — Timbre Mode: Distortion, Filter (noise only), Shape — sets what the TIMBRE fader adjusts; inside Module Modes
Menu — Control Destination — sets which one parameter the CTRL knob and the CTRL input act on, chosen from a list of sixteen covering tune, tone, noise, layer and timbre
Menu — Input Jack S&H — one switch per input jack, plus Set all inputs to use S&H and Set no inputs use S&H; a switched-on input is read only at the instant of a trigger and held until the next
Menu — Quantisation: None, Semitone — rounds the V/OCT input to whole semitones before it is used
Menu — Disable flashing light on trigger — stops the panel lights blinking each time the voice is triggered

Crust.notes: BastlPizza publishes no source, but the installed binary is not stripped: every class and member function keeps its symbol, so Crust::process, processVoiceConfiguration, processCVs, processButtons and CrustWidget::appendContextMenu were all read directly. Everything above came from that disassembly and from the maker's own configParam and configInput descriptions, which are cstring literals in the same binary. Eight of the nineteen parameters sit at one position, the PITCH knob, and three more at the TIMBRE fader and two at the ENV knob: the widget shown is the one the current mode calls for and the others are hidden, so each gets its own line. Crust reads only channel 0 of every input; the channels byte is read at 0x12988 and 0x11504 only to test whether a cable is present. The VELOCITY jack doubles as a gate whenever TRIG is unpatched, with a 1.5V and 0.5V Schmitt pair at 0x11524 and 0x11588 — the maker's tooltips do not mention this. The Input Jack S&H switches are read at 0x12908 onwards, one flag per jack, and skip the CV update on every sample that is not a trigger.

lines: A digital oscillator in which one main oscillator is phase-modulated by either of two others, then wavefolded and ring-modulated, after Bastl's Pizza module
Sets the octave of all the oscillators, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Octave
Detunes the octave oscillator and the ratio oscillator away from the main oscillator: clockwise by an exponential interval, counter-clockwise by a fixed number of Hz whatever the pitch
Shifts the pitch by whole semitones, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Semitone
Shifts the pitch by a fraction of a semitone, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Fine
Sets the pitch freely across the whole frequency range of the oscillator, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Free tune
Sets the top number of the ratio oscillator's frequency ratio, and is what the PITCH knob does after a long press of the ratio oscillator button
Sets the bottom number of the ratio oscillator's frequency ratio, and is what the PITCH knob does after a long press of the ratio oscillator button
Steps the PITCH knob to the next tune mode on each press; a long press swaps between the octave and detune pair and the semitone and fine-tune pair, and a very long press reaches free tune
Sets the depth of phase modulation applied to the main oscillator: no modulation at the centre, the ratio oscillator as modulator to the left and the octave oscillator as modulator to the right
Steps the ratio oscillator through its four stored ratios on each press, named A/B, C/D, E/F and G/H; a long press puts the PITCH knob on the two numbers of the current ratio
Steps the octave oscillator through -1, 0, +1 and +2 octaves relative to the main oscillator on each press
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FM INDEX input before it is added to the FM INDEX knob
Sets how far the waveform is bent away from a sine, and is what the SHAPE knob does while the shape mode is Waveshaping
Sets how far the waveform is folded back on itself, and is what the SHAPE knob does while the shape mode is Wavefolder
Sets the depth of ring modulation applied to the main oscillator, and is what the SHAPE knob does while the shape mode is Ring Modulation
Steps the SHAPE knob to the next shaping mode on each press, through Waveshaping, Wavefolder and Ring Modulation; a long press starts choosing what the CTRL knob is assigned to
Sets whichever one parameter the control destination names, and attenuates the voltage at the CTRL input when a cable is patched there
Adds to whichever shaping amount the SHAPE knob is set to at the moment, -10V to 10V covering the full travel of that knob
Resets the phase of every oscillator on each rising edge, which hard-syncs them and fixes what the attack of an FM sound sounds like
Adds to the CTRL knob, -5V to 5V covering the full range of whatever the control destination names
Adds to the FM INDEX knob through the INDEX MOD attenuverter, -10V to 10V covering the full travel of that knob
Takes the place of the octave oscillator as the modulator of the main oscillator while a cable is patched here, so any signal can phase-modulate the carrier
Sets the pitch of all the oscillators, doubling their frequency for each volt
Carries the square wave of the pulse oscillator at 5V either way, or the ratio oscillator with the envelope applied, whichever the Pulse Out Output menu names
The main oscillator after phase modulation and wave shaping, reaching 5V either way
The octave oscillator on its own, reaching 5V either way
Note — the CTRL knob and the SHAPE, RATIO OSC and OCT OSC buttons each do a second job on a long press, and the light beside the parameter being edited blinks; a second long press returns to normal
Menu — Module Modes — a submenu gathering the mode settings the panel buttons step through
Menu — Tune Mode: Octave, Detune, Semitone, Fine, Free tune — sets what the PITCH knob adjusts; inside Module Modes
Menu — Control Destination — sets which one parameter the CTRL knob and the CTRL input act on, chosen from a list of fourteen covering pitch, detune, the FM ratios and the shaping amounts
Menu — Pulse Out Output: Pulse, Ratio — chooses whether the PULSE jack carries the pulse oscillator or the ratio oscillator
Menu — Ratio Oscillator — a submenu setting the four stored frequency ratios the ratio oscillator button steps through, each shown with the interval it makes
Menu — Quantisation: None, Semitone — rounds the V/OCT input to whole semitones before it is used
Menu — Oversampling — sets how many times over the sample rate the oscillators are run before the result is filtered back down, from Off up to sixteen times

Pizza.notes: BastlPizza publishes no source, but the installed binary keeps its symbols, so Pizza::process, upsampleInputs, AudioHandler_tickAll, processButtons and PizzaWidget::appendContextMenu were read directly. Seven of the seventeen parameters sit at the PITCH knob and three at the SHAPE knob: only the one the current mode calls for is visible, so each has its own line. Every input is read at channel 0 alone; the channels byte is read only to test whether a cable is present. The EXTERNAL input carries no family because what it means is whatever you patch into it — the module uses it as the modulator in place of the octave oscillator, so it can be audio or a control voltage. SYNC has no range field: it is passed to the sync oversampler unscaled at 0x20850 and the threshold is inside Audio_pizza, which was not traced. The PULSE output is only computed when a cable is patched to it, and the envelope is applied to it in Ratio mode but not in Pulse mode.

lines: A stereo delay with diffusion, filtering and extra taps in the feedback path, after Bastl's Basil module
Sets the delay time, longest counter-clockwise and shortest clockwise, and is what the DELAY knob does while the delay mode is Time
Sets the difference between the left and right delay times: identical fully counter-clockwise, and fully clockwise the left grows longer while the right grows shorter
Trims the delay time by a small amount, which tunes the module to a note when the feedback is high enough to ring, and is what the DELAY knob does while the delay mode is Fine
Steps the DELAY knob to the next delay mode on each press, through Time, Stereo and Fine
Crossfades the outputs between the dry input and the delayed signal
Sets how much of the output is fed back in: clockwise the left and right channels each feed back into themselves, counter-clockwise they cross over so the repeats bounce between the two
Halves the sample rate of the delay line on each press, which doubles the delay times and drops the tail an octave; a two-second hold reaches the longer range instead, and the same hold leaves it
Locks the delay buffer into a loop of the set length on each press, cutting the input off so the buffer repeats unchanged; a hold past two seconds also turns the anti-aliasing filter off
Steps the SPACE knob to the next space mode on each press, through Blur, Filter and Taps; a long press starts choosing what the CTRL knob is assigned to
Sets the amount of diffusion: counter-clockwise it happens before the feedback path and adds a gentle low-pass, clockwise it happens inside the feedback path and rings more
Sets the filter in the feedback path, low-pass counter-clockwise and high-pass clockwise, which darkens or brightens each repeat; this is what the SPACE knob does while the space mode is Filter
Mixes in extra taps at delay times shorter than the main one: odd and even divisions counter-clockwise, even divisions alone clockwise; this is what the SPACE knob does while the space mode is Taps
Sets whichever one parameter the control destination names, and adds to the voltage at the CTRL input when a cable is patched there
Adds to whichever space amount the SPACE knob is set to at the moment, -5V to 5V covering the full travel of that knob
Sets the delay time from the interval between two pulses arriving here, measured on each rising edge past 0.2V and smoothed towards the new time
Adds to the CTRL knob, -5V to 5V covering the full range of whatever the control destination names
The left input to the delay; every channel of a polyphonic cable is summed into it
The right input to the delay; every channel of a polyphonic cable is summed into it, and with nothing patched here the left input feeds both sides
Scales the delay time, doubling it for each volt
Adds to the FEEDBACK knob, -5V to 5V covering the full range of that knob
The left output, the dry and delayed signals mixed by the DRY WET knob and reaching 5V either way
The right output, the dry and delayed signals mixed by the DRY WET knob and reaching 5V either way
Note — the module works on blocks of 32 samples, so the controls and the CV inputs are read once every 32 samples rather than every sample
Menu — Hyperspace mode — lifts the limits the module normally puts on the delay time and the feedback
Menu — Anti-aliasing — filters the delay line when it runs at a reduced sample rate; turning it off is what the long press of the FREEZE button also does
Menu — Control Destination — sets which one parameter the CTRL knob and the CTRL input act on, chosen from a list of thirteen covering delay time, feedback, the space amounts and the speed division
Menu — Character: Normal, Half, Quarter, Eighth — sets the sample rate the delay line runs at, the same division the SPEED button steps through

Basil.notes: BastlPizza publishes no source, but the installed binary keeps its symbols, so Basil::process, processButtons, UI_calls, UI_setLEDs, Audio_basil::Sync::triggerIn, AudioHandler::updateAudioParams and BasilWidget::appendContextMenu were read directly. Three of the thirteen parameters sit at the DELAY knob and three more at the SPACE knob: only the one the current mode calls for is visible, so each has its own line. Basil is the only module in this plugin that reads more than channel 0: the left and right inputs each use their channels count as a loop bound at 0x3bc0 and 0x3cc8 and sum every channel into one mono signal, so a polyphonic cable is mixed rather than kept apart. The right input normals to the left. The SYNC threshold of 0.2V is unusually low for a clock input and comes from the comparison at 0x2dfc0 against the constant 0x3e4ccccd; the input is one-pole filtered first. The DELAY input is scaled two to the power of the voltage at 0x398c, but whether a positive voltage lengthens or shortens the delay was not traced past Interpolation::updateValue, so the line says only that it doubles per volt. The Character menu and the SPEED button set the same sample-rate division, which is why the menu names four steps where the button shows two lights.
